title: Credential reference
description: What the rest of AlixAI, and the host application, may know about a provider credential (additive plan section 11.1): an opaque ID, the kind (OAuth or manual API key), a masked fingerprint for manual keys, the status, a safe account identifier, the binding to provider, deployment, application, tenant and permitted scopes, and the times of consent, rotation, validation and revocation. There is no member that can hold a secret: no key, no access or refresh token, no password, no cookie and no key material of any kind; the object is closed, so a secret cannot be added. The secret lives only in the credential service (OS secret store or encrypted file) and is resolved there by ref_id. The fingerprint is the first 8 hex digits of the SHA-256 of the key, never a prefix, suffix or any other part of the key itself. Every member is assembled by the core.

ref_id.description: Opaque credential reference ID. Resolving it to a secret is possible only inside the credential service.

kind.description: oauth: browser-based OAuth authorization (preferred whenever the provider supports it). api_key: manual API key or token entry, a fallback for providers or deployments without a suitable OAuth flow.

label.description: Operator label shown in settings, or null. Never a place for secret material.

binding.description: What the credential is bound to: one provider, one deployment, one application, one tenant and the provider scopes it may be used with. A credential never serves another tenant or provider.

provider_id.description: The provider the credential belongs to.

scopes.description: The provider scopes the credential is permitted to use: the smallest set the selected capability needs. Never empty for oauth; an api_key has no scope concept and may list none.

fingerprint.description: Masked fingerprint of a manual key: sha256: and the first 8 hex digits of its SHA-256. Required for api_key so the operator can tell keys apart; always null for oauth. It cannot be reversed into the key and is too short to identify one across providers.

status.description: pending: not yet validated or authorised. active: validated and usable. expired: past its expiry. revoked: revoked by the operator, the provider or a security reset. invalid: the provider rejected it; fails closed, never triggers an alternate provider. quarantined: the provider reported excessive permissions or an unsupported account policy. reauthorization_required: consent or scopes changed.

account.description: Safe identifiers of the provider account the credential acts for, shown to the host application. Provider-assigned IDs only: never an e-mail address, a name or a secret. Null members are not known.

times.description: Authorization metadata without secret values (additive plan section 11.1). Null: has not happened.

authorized_at.description: When consent was granted (oauth) or the key was entered (api_key).

expires_at.description: When the credential expires: access token expiry for oauth, the operator-set expiry date of a manual key.

rotated_at.description: When the credential was last rotated.

last_validated_at.description: When a minimally scoped provider request last accepted the credential.

warnings.description: Conditions the operator and the host must see. A manual key always carries broader_than_oauth_scopes: it may grant broader access than OAuth scopes.

allOf.description: oauth has no key to fingerprint and always carries at least one provider scope.
A manual key has a masked fingerprint and always warns that it may be broader than OAuth scopes.
A revoked credential records when it was revoked.
A quarantined credential names why: the provider reported excessive permissions or an unsupported account policy.
An active oauth credential records when consent was granted.
An active manual key has been validated with a minimally scoped provider request.
